headline: Medium-risk pair: shared-file and output-to-input pathways can enable prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors; no direct compliance mismatch is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman touches files like CLAUDE.md, project notes, and memory files, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can run browsers. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let document content influence Caveman’s instructions. No direct bridge is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF both agents read from the same workspace or exported files
IF PaddleOCR output is pasted or ingested by Caveman as trusted text
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of OCR output into prompt files
Require manual review before copying outputs
Add provenance tags to generated text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction stripping

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman explicitly touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md; PaddleOCR handles documents and images and has allowlisted network egress. If shared files contain sensitive material, OCR processing plus networked inference can expose it beyond the original workspace. The pairwise leak path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in a shared directory
IF PaddleOCR sends document contents to a remote inference service or API
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared folders
Use local-only OCR for restricted data
Review allowlisted endpoints before processing
Redact secrets before OCR
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP; PaddleOCR runs browsers and has allowlisted egress. Overlap on shared mutable files or browser-driven artifacts could create write conflicts or race conditions, especially if both operate on the same documents or notes. No locking mechanism is documented, so uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or document set
IF browser-generated artifacts are saved back into Caveman-managed files
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file
Avoid concurrent runs on the same project
Snapshot inputs before processing
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content that PaddleOCR could ingest as documents, and PaddleOCR can convert documents into extracted text. If PaddleOCR treats Caveman output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream work products. The interaction is plausible but undocumented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR consumes Caveman-generated notes or markdown without verification
IF downstream users act on extracted text as ground truth
mitigations: Require human verification of extracted facts
Mark generated text as non-authoritative
Keep source documents attached to outputs
Compare OCR output against originals
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and provenance propagation

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and list no special certifications, residency constraints, or secret handling. Caveman touches session logs and memory files, while PaddleOCR touches documents and images, but the profiles do not show a concrete residency or retention mismatch. The other agent is not cited because no compliance divergence is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent
IF one deployment adds retention or residency rules not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
Document retention settings
Confirm storage region for any hosted service
Delete temporary outputs after use
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
